chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Kūfī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ghālib ibn ʿUthmān, from Rūḥ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about vomiting. He said: “There is no wudu (ablution) because of it, even if he vomits deliberately.”

key_terms.الْقَيْءِ: vomiting; the act being asked about in relation to ritual purity
key_terms.تَقَيَّأَ: he vomited; the verbal act under discussion
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu (ablution); the ritual purification required for certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Does vomiting break wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that vomiting does not invalidate wudu (ablution). The ruling applies even when the vomiting is done intentionally, indicating that this act does not require renewing ritual purity for salat (prayer).
